correctness.rationale: Path/vertex equivalence follows from acyclic flow decomposition and the 0–1 extremality argument. Each pair of paths is encoded exactly once by the four-state weighted transition including the final boundary; direct symbolic determinant yields the rational polynomial. A primitive Perron eigenvalue has computed first two derivatives and strictly positive variance, proving the normal limit by analytic perturbation. The standalone exact checker independently enumerates all path pairs through n=12 and verifies the rational recurrence through n=40. The infinite statement is proved analytically, not inferred from the finite checks.

The complete DAG allows jumps of every length; the zigzag DAG forbids jumps of length at least three and uses a distinct uniform vertex measure, so the former unconditional distribution cannot be specialized merely by changing n.
The earlier zigzag order-polytope vertex-degree result counts incident polytope edges, not distances between two uniformly random flow vertices.

originality.rationale: Three directly relevant full primary sources and OEIS were compared for identical objects and stronger implications. Zigzag flow-polytope literature describes vertices/triangulations, not their canonical pairwise Euclidean metric. The potentially strongest Fibonacci-cube Hosoya polynomial concerns a non-isometric Hamming encoding; n=2 distinguishes it explicitly. The previously obtained zigzag local-degree and complete-DAG distance results are mathematically different and do not imply the present restricted-graph uniform-path law. Unindexed priority remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: An uncatalogued or differently worded analysis of symmetric-difference statistics of Fibonacci path incidence vectors may predate this report.
The arXiv lead has a 2026 revised full version: earliest public source is verified 2024-06-28 but the inspected accessible PDF is version two.
No independent external priority certification has been performed.

value.rationale: For a canonical infinite family of convex flow polytopes with exponentially many Fibonacci-enumerated vertices, the claim determines the entire intrinsic edge-coordinate squared-distance distribution in every dimension, not merely its mean. The explicit positive Gaussian variance and unscaled ordinary-Euclidean fluctuation reveal quantitative high-dimensional vertex geometry not captured by face numbers, normalized volume or Fibonacci-cube Hamming geometry. This is a natural, fully motivated metric invariant suitable for geometric comparison.
